title: RAW advance perception alone does not protect unless timely hiding is possible
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_EXECUTED. Megenberg II25 quotes and rejects immunity from prior hearing/seeing, allowing only a qualified possibility of hiding before the strike. Retain quoted authority versus criticism, the same threatened person and the action deadline; no actual escape or guaranteed safety is asserted.

design.mechanism: The source attributes to our book a universal immunity claim for a person who hears or sees thunder/lightning before the strike reaches that person. The author rejects its warrant and says advance perception does not help unless the person could hide sufficiently quickly before the strike. Keep attributed claim, authorial criticism, the same potential victim/percipient/hider, and the conditional action deadline distinct. Information alone is not equated with enacted protection.
design.contrast: R1: author and quoted book jointly endorse unconditional immunity. R2: seeing or hearing the event itself physically protects the observer. R3: hiding at any time is equivalent to hiding before the strike. R4: the warning recipient, potential hider and threatened person are interchangeable individuals. R5: a conditional possibility of timely hiding asserts that hiding occurs or guarantees safety. R6: two sensory alternatives are two observed protective successes.
design.prediction: A faithful account must let the book assert the broad immunity claim while the author withholds it: prior hearing/seeing alone does not supply the missing action. The possible helpful exception depends on the threatened person being able to hide before the strike arrives. Deleting the action or moving its deadline after arrival changes the qualified criticism into the very immunity claim it disputes. This is an attributed argument with a guarded possibility, not a positive report of a successful escape.
whole_source_duties: Exact complete local unit93.32 beginning ez spricht unser puoch through94.1 ending vor dem slag verpergen. The next ez spricht auch daz puoch starts a different attributed claim and is outside this local argument.

The quoted claim concerns thunder or lightning, prior hearing OR seeing, the strike coming to the person, and nobody being harmed under that prior-perception condition. Do not erase the universal scope of the attributed claim.
The author calls that assertion an unlearned/light saying and says our foreseeing does not help. The exception is expressed through the person being able to hide quickly enough before the strike.
The exception is modal and conditional. It does not state that anyone actually hides, that warning is always sufficient for hiding, or that every hiding place reliably protects.
Hearing and seeing are alternative routes to advance perception here. They are not two measured cases and do not by themselves demonstrate source-side repeated protective success.
Earlier91.31–92.11 distinguishes visual/auditory order and absent sensory access; those duties establish nearby context but are not imported as an extra mechanism proving safety.

Immediately preceding93.25–32 has Marcia/child differential harm; immediately following94.1–7 gives further attributed mortality/eagle/laurel assertions. These remain historical context and must not be merged into an inferred universal immunity or silently corrected to familiar lore.
Full chapter retains its causal, selective-harm, analogy, season/place and classification duties. This RAW is one contiguous criticism, not a claim to render the whole chapter or current588.
